method: pymatgen get_element_profile(Li, SE) (open-Li, same as esw_grand_potential); reaction at V~0 (mu_Li=metal) = Li-metal reduction interphase. leaky_products = phases with MP gap < 2.0 eV (electron-conducting -> non-passivating). MP GGA/GGA+U. Compare b2o3 vs LPSCl1.6.

b2o3.anode_reduction_reaction: Li58B2P8S41Cl16O3 -> 2 LiB + 3 Li2O + 8 Li3P + 16 LiCl + 41 S + 10 Li

interpretation: Both SEs are Li-metal-UNSTABLE (reduce to Li3P 0.7 eV leaky, sulfide-generic). BUT b2o3's B dopant ADDS a METALLIC LiB phase (gap 0.0) to the anode interphase -> min gap 0.0 vs undoped 0.7 -> doping WORSENS Li-metal electronic stability. b2o3 also adds Li2O (4.9, passivating). Net: b2o3 needs an anode interlayer more than undoped. Thermodynamic products only; morphology/kinetics not modeled.
